_source_note: Cloud-relevant subset of the MITRE ATT&CK Enterprise matrix (STIX 2.1 technique IDs, names, and tactics), bundled as a static snapshot for offline embedding — not a live feed. ~30 techniques covering the tactics most relevant to CSPM findings (initial access through impact).

techniques.name: Valid Accounts
techniques.description: An adversary obtains and abuses credentials of an existing cloud account to gain initial access, maintain persistence, or escalate privileges, often bypassing detections aimed at malware because the activity uses legitimate credentials.

techniques.name: Exploit Public-Facing Application
techniques.description: An adversary exploits a weakness in an internet-facing application, storage bucket, or service that is misconfigured to allow public access, gaining a foothold or direct access to stored data without authentication.

techniques.name: Account Manipulation
techniques.description: An adversary modifies account permissions, adds credentials, or attaches an overly permissive or wildcard policy granting broad or unrestricted access to a single IAM role or user, in order to maintain access to a compromised cloud identity, such as attaching an administrator policy to a role they control.

techniques.name: Create Account
techniques.description: An adversary creates a new cloud identity, such as an IAM user or service account, to maintain access to the environment independent of any compromised account that might be discovered and revoked.

techniques.name: Modify Authentication Process
techniques.description: An adversary modifies an authentication mechanism, such as disabling multi-factor authentication requirements or altering a trust policy, to ensure continued access or lower the bar for future access.

techniques.name: Abuse Elevation Control Mechanism
techniques.description: An adversary circumvents controls meant to limit privilege, such as assuming a role with broader permissions than their current identity or exploiting an overly permissive trust relationship between roles.

techniques.name: Domain or Tenant Policy Modification
techniques.description: An adversary modifies organization-wide or tenant-wide policies, such as service control policies, permission boundaries, or account-wide guardrails, to weaken restrictions across an entire cloud organization or multiple accounts, rather than granting excess permission to a single identity.

techniques.name: Impair Defenses
techniques.description: An adversary disables or degrades security tooling, such as turning off CloudTrail logging, disabling GuardDuty, or removing a security group rule that was blocking their activity, to operate without detection.

techniques.name: Modify Cloud Compute Infrastructure
techniques.description: An adversary creates, deletes, or modifies compute resources such as EC2 instances or snapshots to evade defenses, hide their activity, or establish infrastructure for follow-on actions.

techniques.name: Modify Cloud Resource Hierarchy
techniques.description: An adversary moves a resource between accounts, organizational units, or projects to evade security controls, logging, or monitoring scoped to the resource's original location in the cloud hierarchy.

techniques.name: Indicator Removal
techniques.description: An adversary deletes or tampers with logs, such as clearing CloudTrail history or disabling log file validation, to remove evidence of their activity in the cloud environment.

techniques.name: Unsecured Credentials
techniques.description: An adversary searches for credentials stored in plaintext, such as access keys embedded in code, environment variables, or the instance metadata service, and uses them to gain unauthorized access.

techniques.name: Credentials from Password Stores
techniques.description: An adversary accesses a secrets manager, credential vault, or password store to harvest stored secrets and use them for further access into the cloud environment.

techniques.name: Multi-Factor Authentication Request Generation
techniques.description: An adversary who already possesses primary credentials repeatedly generates MFA push notifications to a legitimate user, hoping to prompt an accidental approval that grants them full access.

techniques.name: Cloud Service Discovery
techniques.description: An adversary enumerates the cloud services enabled in an account, such as listing available APIs or querying which regions and services are active, to understand the environment before further action.

techniques.name: Cloud Infrastructure Discovery
techniques.description: An adversary enumerates cloud infrastructure such as instances, storage buckets, databases, and networking configuration to map out the environment and identify high-value targets.

techniques.name: Container and Resource Discovery
techniques.description: An adversary enumerates containers, clusters, or serverless functions running in the environment to identify workloads that might hold sensitive data or provide a path to further access.

techniques.name: Cloud Storage Object Discovery
techniques.description: An adversary lists the contents of cloud storage buckets or containers to identify files of interest, such as backups, credentials, or customer data, ahead of a collection or exfiltration step.

techniques.name: Cloud Service Dashboard
techniques.description: An adversary accesses a cloud provider's management console or dashboard using compromised credentials to visually explore the account's configuration and resources.

techniques.name: Permission Groups Discovery
techniques.description: An adversary enumerates IAM groups, roles, and their attached policies to identify accounts with elevated privileges suitable for further compromise or lateral movement.

techniques.name: Account Discovery
techniques.description: An adversary enumerates the IAM users, roles, and service accounts that exist within the cloud environment to identify targets for credential theft or privilege escalation.

techniques.name: Use Alternate Authentication Material
techniques.description: An adversary uses a stolen session token, application access token, or temporary security credential to authenticate as another identity without needing that identity's primary credentials.

techniques.name: Data from Cloud Storage
techniques.description: An adversary accesses data directly from cloud storage services such as object storage buckets or managed databases, often via APIs, to collect information prior to exfiltration.

techniques.name: Data from Information Repositories
techniques.description: An adversary collects sensitive data from a shared repository such as a wiki, ticketing system, or code repository hosted in the cloud environment.

techniques.name: Transfer Data to Cloud Account
techniques.description: An adversary moves data from a compromised cloud account into a storage resource in an account they control, exfiltrating it while it still appears to be normal intra-cloud traffic.

techniques.name: Exfiltration Over Web Service
techniques.description: An adversary exfiltrates data over an external web service, such as an anonymous file-sharing site or a webhook endpoint, to blend the transfer in with ordinary outbound web traffic.

techniques.name: Data Destruction
techniques.description: An adversary permanently deletes data, storage buckets, or database tables in the cloud environment, aiming to disrupt operations or destroy evidence of prior compromise.

techniques.name: Data Encrypted for Impact
techniques.description: An adversary encrypts data in cloud storage or databases and withholds the decryption key, rendering the resource unusable until a ransom is paid or the data is restored from backup.

techniques.name: Inhibit System Recovery
techniques.description: An adversary deletes backups, disables versioning, or removes snapshots to prevent the victim from recovering data or infrastructure after a destructive or ransomware-style attack.

techniques.name: Escape to Host
techniques.description: An adversary breaks out of a container or serverless execution environment to gain access to the underlying host or the broader cloud account's credentials and resources.
